summary: Today’s PaymentsDive recap: 8 new stories, with focus on regulation, product + fintech innovation.

articles.title: PayPal’s new CFO lands big pay
articles.description: The digital payments player handed Claire Bramley, an HP alum, a $30 million pay package to take the chief financial officer post in February.

articles.title: Fed President pitches FedNow
articles.description: Jeff Schmid, who leads the Kansas City Federal Reserve, nudged credit union executives last week to adopt faster payment options, like FedNow.

articles.title: Trump signs Common Cents bill
articles.description: The new law gives merchants a legal basis for rounding retail cash transactions as pennies disappear.

articles.title: How digital dollars improve cross-border payment management
articles.description: As businesses look for more dependable ways to pay partners across borders, digital dollars are an emerging option.

articles.title: Travel brands aren’t the only ones that benefit from non-prime credit card partnerships
articles.description: 75% of non-prime consumers plan to travel. Here's how brands can earn their loyalty.

articles.title: PayPal CEO remakes team
articles.description: Chief Financial Officer Jamie Miller, who served as the digital payment company’s interim CEO at one point, will leave as CEO Enrique Lores installs new managers.

articles.title: Bill sells for $6B to TPG, Corpay
articles.description: The deal for the bill-pay company fuels consolidation in the business payments and receivables software industry.

articles.title: M&T aims to ‘dial up’ credit card rewards
articles.description: The regional lender is looking to offer simple and easy-to-understand credit card perks, in line with recent customer feedback.
